note: NAMED WALLETS — durable destinations we save permanently (Jordan, 2026-09-15). Refer to a wallet by NAME instead of pasting an address. Names are stable; addresses are the thing that changes. This file is the human-facing layer; capital-guard-rails.json remains the enforcement layer. A name here does NOT authorize a transfer by itself - the guard still checks the address.
principle: Name the destination, not the address. Exchange addresses rotate; named wallets do not.

jordan.label: Jordan (personal)
jordan.purpose: Primary personal wallet - long-term savings, bills, personal use
jordan.notes: The GTA remit target (gta_close_executor.py REMIT_TARGET). Durable - save permanently.

gentech-labs.label: GenTech Labs (x402 seller signer)
gentech-labs.purpose: x402 gateway payTo / seller signer on Base
gentech-labs.notes: Verified on-chain. Approved rail for x402 payouts.

transient.note: One-time receive addresses that must NOT be saved as durable. Exchange deposit addresses rotate, so each new address needs a fresh orchestrator approval. Recorded here for audit history only.

coinbase-deposit-2026-09-15.label: Coinbase deposit (rotating)
coinbase-deposit-2026-09-15.notes: Coinbase rotates deposit addresses. Jordan: 'sometimes I may send you a wallet and say send to this wallet, but it's just Coinbase.' NEVER reuse without a fresh approval.

usage: Jordan says 'send to jordan' -> resolve the name, show the address, execute
Jordan pastes a raw address -> treat as TRANSIENT; approve for that one move only
Adding a durable wallet: create a block under wallets, give it a label + purpose
Adding a rotating exchange address: put it under transient, never under wallets
